steps: ATP means adenosine triphosphate; ADP means adenosine diphosphate.
ATP and ADP are energy-carrying molecules present in cells.
ATP stores energy and supplies it for cellular activities when it changes into ADP and phosphate.
ADP can be changed back into ATP by adding a phosphate group, using energy released during respiration.
items.finalAnswer: ATP stands for adenosine triphosphate and ADP for adenosine diphosphate; ATP stores and supplies energy for cellular activities by breaking down into ADP and phosphate, while ADP can be converted back into ATP.

steps: Respiration is the breakdown of food, especially glucose, in cells to release energy.
Aerobic respiration is the breakdown of food in the presence of oxygen to release energy.
Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of food in the absence of oxygen to release energy.
items.finalAnswer: Respiration is the breakdown of food to release energy; aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen, whereas anaerobic respiration occurs in its absence.

steps: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the chief energy currency of all cells.
Energy released during respiration is stored in ATP and can be supplied to cellular activities when needed.
When ATP breaks down by hydrolysis into ADP (adenosine diphosphate) and inorganic phosphate, energy is released.
ADP combines with phosphate, using energy, to form ATP again.
items.finalAnswer: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the chief energy currency of all cells; it supplies energy when it breaks down by hydrolysis into ADP (adenosine diphosphate) and phosphate.

steps: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts of green cells, where chlorophyll absorbs light energy.
Light energy is converted into chemical energy.
Water molecules are split into hydrogen and oxygen using light energy; oxygen is released.
Hydrogen combines with carbon dioxide to form glucose, storing chemical energy in the food.
The overall process can be represented as: carbon dioxide + water — light and chlorophyll → glucose + oxygen.
items.finalAnswer: In photosynthesis, chlorophyll absorbs light and converts its energy into chemical energy; water is split into hydrogen and oxygen, oxygen is released, and hydrogen combines with carbon dioxide to form glucose.

steps: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose in the absence of oxygen, releasing a small amount of energy.
In yeast, glucose is converted into ethanol and carbon dioxide; this process is called alcoholic fermentation.
Alcoholic fermentation is used in baking, because carbon dioxide makes dough rise, and in brewing, to produce alcoholic drinks.
In muscle cells during strenuous exercise, glucose is converted into lactic acid when the oxygen supply is insufficient; this is lactic acid fermentation.
Lactic acid fermentation also occurs in certain bacteria and is used to make yoghurt and other fermented milk products.
items.finalAnswer: The two types of anaerobic respiration are alcoholic fermentation, in which yeast converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide (used in baking and brewing), and lactic acid fermentation, in which muscle cells or certain bacteria convert glucose into lactic acid (important in strenuous exercise and used to make yoghurt and other fermented milk products).

steps: Aerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose in the presence of oxygen to release energy.
It takes place in stages: glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm, while the later stages occur in the mitochondria.
During glycolysis, one glucose molecule is broken down into two molecules of pyruvic acid, releasing a small amount of energy.
In the mitochondria, pyruvic acid is further broken down in the presence of oxygen; carbon dioxide and water are formed, and much more energy is released.
The released energy is stored in ATP.
items.finalAnswer: In aerobic respiration, glycolysis breaks glucose into pyruvic acid in the cytoplasm; pyruvic acid is then further broken down in the mitochondria in the presence of oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water, releasing energy stored in ATP.

steps: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to make glucose and oxygen; respiration uses glucose and oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water.
Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts containing chlorophyll; respiration begins in the cytoplasm and its later stages occur in mitochondria.
Photosynthesis requires light and stores energy in glucose; respiration does not require light and releases energy from glucose.
Photosynthesis occurs in green cells; respiration occurs in all living cells.
Thus, the raw materials and products of the two processes are broadly opposite.
items.finalAnswer: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts of green cells and requires light to use carbon dioxide and water to make glucose and oxygen, storing energy; respiration occurs in all living cells, begins in the cytoplasm and continues in mitochondria, uses glucose and oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water, and releases energy without requiring light.

steps: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) consists of adenine, ribose sugar and three phosphate groups.
Energy is associated with the bonds between its phosphate groups, especially the bond to the terminal phosphate.
When the terminal phosphate is removed by hydrolysis, ATP forms ADP (adenosine diphosphate) and inorganic phosphate, releasing energy for cellular activities.
ADP can be converted back into ATP by the addition of a phosphate group using energy from respiration or photosynthesis.
items.finalAnswer: ATP’s three phosphate groups allow energy to be stored in their bonds; hydrolysis removes the terminal phosphate to form ADP and inorganic phosphate, releasing energy, and energy from respiration or photosynthesis can add the phosphate back.
